newsitem.title: USA: Four charged with attempted murder in UPS incident.
newsitem.headline: Four charged with attempted murder in UPS incident.

text.p: Miami police have charged three United Parcel Service strikers with attempted murder for allegedly attacking a UPS employee with an icepick as he made deliveries, police said Monday.
A fourth man was charged with aggravated battery.
Roderick Carter, working in defiance of a strike by 185,000 workers at the nation's largest package carrier, was attacked Thursday when his UPS truck stopped at a traffic light.
Several men surrounded the vehicle and tried to slash its tyres. Carter jumped from his cab and, in a struggle, he was stabbed five times with an icepick, the police report said.
Police arrested four men over the weekend, police spokeswoman Nina Fonticiella said.
Angel Mielgo, 30, Orestes Espinosa, 30, and Benigno Rojas, 28, were charged with attempted murder. Adran Paez, 25, was charged with aggravated battery.
"All are UPS workers," Fonticiella said, adding that they were being held in jail. "This is the only incident we've had like this but tension is mounting," she said.
Carter, 31, a former University of Miami football star, was released from the hospital after spending Thursday night under observation.

A Miami Judge granted UPS an injunction Friday barring the Teamsters union from interfering in the company's operations. The injunction applies only in Dade County, which encompasses the urban Miami area.

The union represents 185,000 workers nationwide who sort, load, pickup and deliver shipments in UPS vans. It is demanding better health and pension benefits, higher pay and restrictions on part-time workers and non-union subcontractors. The strike is in its eighth day.
